name: Exact Sciences Corp

profile.description: Exact Sciences was a cancer screening and diagnostics company headquartered in Madison, Wisconsin. Its flagship product Cologuard is the dominant non-invasive stool-based DNA test for colorectal cancer screening, complemented by Cologuard Plus (next-generation test), Oncotype DX genomic tests for breast and colon cancer treatment guidance, and pipeline products including CancerGuard (multi-cancer early detection) and OncoDetect (minimal residual disease monitoring). Abbott Laboratories acquired Exact Sciences for $105 per share in cash ($21B equity value, $23B enterprise value), closing on March 23, 2026 [4]. FY2025 revenue was $3.25B (up 18% YoY). This report reflects pre-acquisition fundamentals.

innovation.label: STRONG
innovation.analysis: Track Record (2/3): Exact Sciences successfully expanded from a single-product company (Cologuard) to a multi-product diagnostics platform through the 2019 Genomic Health acquisition ($2.8B for Oncotype DX) and launched Cologuard Plus with improved sensitivity [1]. Revenue grew from $2.08B in 2022 to $3.25B in 2025 (56% growth in 3 years), and Q1 2026 continued growing 12% YoY to approximately $878M before the Abbott acquisition closed [1]. The Abbott acquisition at $105/share validated the platform's value. AI Deployment (1/2): CEO Kevin Conroy stated AI will impact 'every new diagnostic the company brings to physicians and patients,' and machine learning is used in genomic analysis pipelines for Oncotype DX and CancerGuard [2]. However, no specific quantified AI revenue or cost savings reported. Market Share (2/2): Cologuard is the dominant non-invasive colorectal cancer screening test with expanded Medicare coverage and growing physician adoption. Oncotype DX is the standard-of-care genomic test for breast cancer treatment decisions, recommended in major clinical guidelines [1]. Pipeline (2/2): CancerGuard multi-cancer early detection test and OncoDetect minimal residual disease monitoring have specific development timelines. The company targeted 15% compounded revenue growth through 2027 with $150M+ in annual cost savings, now pursued under Abbott's umbrella [1]. R&D Intensity (0/1): R&D spending is substantial but consistent with diagnostics industry peers rather than above-average.

inspiration.label: STRONG
inspiration.analysis: Mission Floor (3/4): Exact Sciences' purpose of 'eradicating cancer through earlier detection' is specific, thoughtful, and deeply connected to the company's product strategy — every product directly advances the mission of catching cancer when it is most treatable [2]. CEO Kevin Conroy led the company for 16 years with consistent focus on this mission, guiding strategic decisions from Cologuard development through Genomic Health acquisition and into multi-cancer detection. The mission is idealistic and service-oriented in a way few corporate purposes achieve. Community Impact (2/2): The company directly saves lives through cancer screening — Cologuard has enabled millions of people to be screened who might otherwise skip colonoscopies, making cancer detection more accessible and affordable [1]. This is genuine community impact aligned with the core business and Kingdom-building values. Employee Retention (1/2): Glassdoor rating of 3.6/5 with 1,169+ reviews; career development programs and mentorship cited positively, though Comparably rates the executive team in the bottom 20% of similar-size companies, and reviews describe bureaucratic culture and management paralysis [2]. Insider Buying (1/2): CEO Conroy's 16-year tenure with $49.5M in total compensation (97.8% equity-based) shows significant skin in the game through stock ownership aligned with shareholders [2]. The Abbott acquisition at $105/share validated this alignment. No evidence of meaningful open-market purchases beyond compensation.

infrastructure.label: DEVELOPING
infrastructure.analysis: Mechanically scored on growth-stock metrics using pre-acquisition data. D/E of 105.6% is above the 70% target but below the 300% floor, scoring 0.85 — the company carries $2.5B in debt from acquisitions [3]. ROE of -8.7% scores at floor, reflecting ongoing GAAP net losses despite $3.25B revenue [3]. Revenue growth of 18% YoY (FY2025) and 16.1% 5-year CAGR both exceed the 10% target, scoring at 1.0 [1]. Forward P/E of 55.2 is near the 60 floor, scoring 0.12 — the pre-acquisition valuation reflected significant future profitability expectations [3]. Profit margin of -6.4% scores at floor — GAAP unprofitable due to acquisition-related amortization despite $282M in free cash flow [3]. PEG unavailable, excluded. Weighted calculation: (1x0.85 + 2x0.0 + 1x1.0 + 2x1.0 + 1x0.12 + 1x0.0) / 8 x 10 = 4.96 rounded to 5.

ai_resilience.label: MODERATE
ai_resilience.analysis: AI Risk Protection (5/9): Exact Sciences operates in molecular diagnostics — a regulated, lab-based business requiring FDA-approved tests, CLIA-certified laboratories, and physician orders [1]. These regulatory barriers create meaningful defenses that AI alone cannot bypass. However, AI poses real competitive threat: AI-powered liquid biopsy companies (Guardant Health's Shield blood test, Grail's Galleri multi-cancer test) could develop AI-driven cancer screening that proves more convenient than stool-based collection, potentially eroding Cologuard's market position [1]. AI also enables faster development of competing multi-cancer detection tests, intensifying pipeline competition. The company's proprietary biomarker databases from millions of tests provide defensibility, but the diagnostic platform is not immune to AI-enabled disruption in screening modalities. AI Opportunity (1/1): Exact Sciences leverages machine learning in its genomic analysis pipelines for Oncotype DX scoring and CancerGuard development. CEO Conroy has explicitly stated AI will impact development of 'every new diagnostic' the company brings to market [2]. AI is integral to next-generation product development.

infinite_game.summary: Exact Sciences under Kevin Conroy's 16-year leadership demonstrated strong infinite game characteristics — a clear Just Cause of eradicating cancer through earlier detection that consistently guided strategic decisions from Cologuard development through the Genomic Health acquisition and into multi-cancer detection. The company invested for long-term capability even at the expense of near-term profitability. Abbott's acquisition at $21B validates the platform's enduring value but raises questions about whether the Just Cause will persist under new ownership focused on portfolio returns.

just_cause.analysis: Just Cause (3/3): 'Eradicating cancer through earlier detection' is a genuine Just Cause by Sinek's definition — resilient (endures beyond any single product), inclusive (invites patients, physicians, and payers to participate), service-oriented (benefits millions of patients), idealistic (a future where cancer is caught early enough to cure), and big (can never be fully achieved) [2]. CEO Conroy's 16-year tenure pursuing this mission through multiple product generations (Cologuard, Cologuard Plus, CancerGuard) validates it through consistent execution across market cycles. Strategic decisions — acquiring Genomic Health for $2.8B, investing in multi-cancer detection, accepting years of GAAP losses to build the platform — all trace back to this cause.

trusting_teams.analysis: Trusting Teams (1/2): Exact Sciences maintained a 3.6/5 Glassdoor rating with 1,169+ reviews; positive feedback on career development programs, mentorship, and continuing education [2]. However, critical reviews describe middle management 'paralyzed by fear of rocking the boat' with upper leadership rewarding 'compliance over competence' and innovation being 'smothered by endless slide decks.' Comparably rates the executive team in the bottom 20% of similar-size companies [2]. This suggests adequate but not exceptional trust — the mission inspires employees individually but organizational bureaucracy limits the Circle of Safety.

worthy_rivals.analysis: Worthy Rivals (1/1): Exact Sciences operated alongside formidable competitors — Guardant Health in liquid biopsy, Grail/Illumina in multi-cancer early detection, and traditional colonoscopy providers. The company acknowledged competitors' strengths and used competitive pressure to improve its own products, launching Cologuard Plus with enhanced sensitivity in response to advancing liquid biopsy technologies [1]. The Genomic Health acquisition showed willingness to build complementary capabilities rather than pursuing a 'win at all costs' strategy.

existential_flexibility.analysis: Existential Flexibility (1/2): Exact Sciences evolved from a single-product colorectal cancer screening company to a multi-product cancer diagnostics platform. The $2.8B Genomic Health acquisition in 2019 expanded into treatment guidance (Oncotype DX), and the CancerGuard and OncoDetect pipeline represented further evolution toward comprehensive cancer diagnostics [1]. The acceptance of the Abbott acquisition itself can be viewed as flexibility — choosing to advance the mission through a larger platform rather than remaining independent. These are meaningful but incremental extensions of the core diagnostic capability.

courage_to_lead.analysis: Courage to Lead (1/2): Kevin Conroy invested heavily in Cologuard commercialization for years before achieving scale, and the $2.8B Genomic Health acquisition was a bold diversification bet [2]. The company accepted GAAP losses for over a decade to invest in multi-cancer detection and platform building rather than cutting R&D for near-term profitability. The decision to sell to Abbott at $105/share — while potentially limiting the company's independent future — provided certain value to shareholders and ensured the mission would continue with Abbott's global distribution capabilities. However, the 16-year path to profitability tests the limits of courage versus necessity.

investment_thesis: Exact Sciences was a cancer diagnostics leader that generated $3.25B in FY2025 revenue (up 18% YoY) with Cologuard dominating non-invasive colorectal cancer screening and Oncotype DX as standard-of-care breast cancer genomics [1]. Abbott Laboratories acquired the company for $105 per share in cash ($21B equity value) on March 23, 2026, ending Exact Sciences' run as an independent public company [4]. The acquisition validated the platform at approximately 6.5x trailing revenue. Under Abbott's ownership, Exact Sciences' products benefit from global distribution infrastructure while continuing the CancerGuard multi-cancer detection and OncoDetect minimal residual disease pipeline. Operating cash flow of $491M and free cash flow of $282M demonstrated the underlying business was approaching sustainable profitability despite GAAP losses from acquisition-related amortization [3]. CEO Conroy's 16-year mission of 'eradicating cancer through earlier detection' now continues through Abbott's diagnostics portfolio.
thesis_continued: The stock is no longer independently tradeable following the Abbott acquisition at $105/share on March 23, 2026 [4]. For investors who held through the acquisition, the key question was whether $105 represented fair value — the premium of approximately 30% to the pre-announcement price reflected Abbott's strategic interest but some analysts believed the multi-cancer detection pipeline was worth significantly more if developed independently. Pre-acquisition bear case risks included: the company remained GAAP unprofitable after 30 years with -6.4% net margins and $2.5B in debt from acquisitions [3]; competition from Guardant Health's Shield blood-based test and Grail's Galleri multi-cancer test could erode Cologuard's market position if liquid biopsy proves more convenient than stool-based screening [1]; and Comparably-rated executive team in the bottom 20% suggested cultural challenges at scale [2]. These risks were effectively resolved by the Abbott acquisition, which provided downside protection at $105/share.
key_catalysts: Abbott acquisition closed at $105/share on March 23, 2026 — stock is no longer independently traded; future catalysts accrue to Abbott (ABT) shareholders
CancerGuard multi-cancer early detection test development continues under Abbott's umbrella with access to global distribution infrastructure and clinical validation resources
Cologuard Plus continued adoption with improved sensitivity driving higher physician conversion rates, now leveraging Abbott's established healthcare relationships worldwide
key_risks: Abbott integration risk — maintaining Exact Sciences' innovation culture and mission focus within a $200B+ conglomerate that optimizes across diverse healthcare portfolio businesses

Liquid biopsy disruption continues — Guardant Health's Shield blood test and Grail's Galleri position blood-based screening as potentially more convenient than stool-based Cologuard, regardless of ownership
GAAP profitability of the Exact Sciences segment within Abbott remains uncertain — pre-acquisition -6.4% net margins and $2.5B in acquired debt create ongoing financial drag on the combined entity
